globalfastener prints TWO hub depths: "t2 Hub Groove, loose, min=nominal" (1.0, 1.4, 1.8 ...) and "t2 Hub Groove, Tight" (0.5, 0.9, 1.2 ...). fasten.it ("groove depth t2", drawing d1+t2) and AVSLD ("Hub Keyway Depth d = t2", printed d + x) print one unqualified t2 and never say it is the loose/back-clearance depth; matching them to the "loose" row is done by the numbers. Lead rule: every counted page must mean the same t2, otherwise the column goes. Numerically the loose values agree on GF, FI, AV for all 20 rows (no rival).

shape_hint: A straight bar of rectangular cross-section b x h (square up to 6 x 6) that sits half in a keyway milled into the shaft (depth t1) and half in a keyway in the hub bore (depth t2); form A has both ends rounded with radius b/2, form B has square ends.

notes: Candidate 20 sizes x 8 columns -> kept 20 x 6 (b, h, shaft over / to, t1, t2). Three unrelated clusters carry all six columns for all 20 sizes: globalfastener (DIN 6885 A/B 1968 and DIN 6885-1 A/B 2021 pages; fullerfasteners is the same template), fasten.it (DIN 6885-1, 08/1968 sheet) and AVSLD International (distributor table of keys and keyways to DIN 6885/1 next to DIN 6885/3). Further agreeing pages: Impex Industrial blog chart (all sizes), National Machine Tool chart (to 32x18), fasteners.eu (b, h, shaft range from 4x4; no depths), boltsfastener (depths only to 20x12), schrauben-lexikon (h and shaft range to 45x25), woodstockindustrial and vibromera (size pairs only). The Impex and National Machine Tool pages are recent blog-style pages; no kept cell depends on them (every kept cell has globalfastener + fasten.it + AVSLD). t2 is the hub keyway depth WITH back clearance (globalfastener: "Hub Groove, loose, min = nominal size"); AVSLD prints it as "d + t2". t1 and t2 are the lower limits / nominal depths; tolerances (+0.1 / +0.2 / +0.3) are not in the table. fasten.it marks DIN 6885-1 (1968) as withdrawn; globalfastener shows identical numbers on its 1968 and 2021 pages. KS B 1311 / JIS B 1301 were not compared. The key drawing in the site uses lMin as a fallback length; with lMin dropped the drawing needs a chosen length.
